title: The Dark Mountain Route
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Edogawa, Ayumi Yoshida, Genta, Mitsuhiko, Haibara, Professor Agasa, Detective Takagi, Inspector) omitted by convention -- their in-story function (the horse-thistle-transfer clue picked up on Ayumi Yoshida's pants while Eiko slept beside her, and Agasa's kerosene-smell deduction) is preserved as clue content rather than as person nodes. The old case file's stated culprit (Eiko Ikeguchi, s1) is CONFIRMED correct against the transcript -- unlike some other rebuilds, this one holds up. Corrections made against the old file: (1) the old file gave Eiko ownership of the weather balloon; the transcript makes clear the balloons belonged to Hayashida (a weather-station employee doing legitimate survey work) and Eiko secretly took six of them without permission -- ownership/theft direction was backwards. (2) the old file used a single generic 'weather balloon' object and a single 'Mountain' location; the transcript supports six balloons used together (five released to drift north to a lake, one kept, deflated and cut), and at least six functionally distinct locations (cottage, cliff base/crime scene, cliff top/launch point, forest 3km away, the lake, and Hayashida's claimed survey site on a neighboring mountain). (3) the old file omitted Motoki entirely as a node even though he is the entire motive engine of the case (Eiko's secretly-dating boyfriend, dead 3 years prior after Hayashida withheld a safety warning out of jealousy) -- added as a backstory_figure. (4) added Ashizuka's on-screen accusatory motive against Takemi ('That's why Motoki-san is dead, too') as a red-herring has_motive_against edge, which the old file's flat suspect list did not capture. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: A horse thistle that only grows in the forest 3km away turned up on a companion's pants, transferred from Eiko while they slept side by side -- proof Eiko had been in the forest despite her alibi.

Strange footprints on the mid-cliff rocks point toward the edge, and a rope-mark/blood scrape sits at the cliff top -- consistent only with someone light enough to descend balloon-slowed and climb back up in a hurry.
Kerosene from the balloon coating clings to anyone who handles them: Hayashida, who says he did the surveying, has no trace of it; Eiko reeks of it.

edges.detail: knew Motoki was heading toward the dangerous cliff top but said nothing, out of jealousy over Eiko and Motoki's relationship
